_README: Hand-verified coordinates for scraped-directory entries whose street address
WHY THIS EXISTS: rural Alaska addresses are often 'Mile 96.5 Parks Highway' or
a PO box, which Nominatim cannot resolve. scrape_acoa.py used to silently fall
back to geocoding the TOWN, storing e.g. Montana Creek Campground at the centre
of Willow -- 39.6 km from the campground. Eight records shipped that way and one
of them (Palmer/Anchorage N. KOA, on Palmer's exact coordinates) was found in the
field. There is no 'approximate' concept in this app: a place is either where it
says it is, or it does not ship.
Keys are the exact address string the scraper builds, so a lookup here happens
BEFORE any geocoding. Every entry must carry a `source` that a reviewer can check.
If an address resolves to nothing here and nothing at street level, the record is
DROPPED rather than degraded to its town. Producing a machine-readable list of
such drops is v2.0 pipeline work.
